title.en: Define i and a complex number a + ib

say.en: No real number squared gives minus 1, so x squared plus 1 equals 0 has no real solution. Mathematicians simply invented one: i. In this lesson: Define i and a complex number a plus ib.
Find real and imaginary parts.
Simplify powers of i.

title.en: The imaginary unit and complex numbers

body.en: Let $i = \sqrt{-1}$, so $i^2 = -1$. A complex number is $z = a + ib$ with $a, b$ real: $a = \text{Re}(z)$ is the real part and $b = \text{Im}(z)$ the *imaginary* part. $a + ib = c + id$ only when $a = c$ and $b = d$. Powers of $i$ repeat in fours: $i, -1, -i, 1$.
body.kn: i = √−1, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ i² = −1. ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ z = a + ib; a ವಾಸ್ತವ ಭಾಗ, b ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಭಾಗ. i ಯ ಘಾತಗಳು ನಾಲ್ಕರ ಚಕ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find i⁻³⁹.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find i to the power minus 39.
i to the power minus 39 equals 1 over i to the power 39, and 39 equals 4 times 9 plus 3, so i to the power 39 equals i cubed equals -i.
1 over (-i) equals minus 1 over i equals -i over i squared equals i.
So the answer is i.

problem.en: Find real x and y if (3x − 2) + i(y + 4) = 7 − 2i.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find real x and y if (3x − 2) + i(y + 4) = 7 − 2i.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find real x and y if 3x minus 2 plus iy plus 4 equals 7 minus 2i.
Equate real parts: 3x minus 2 equals 7 so x equals 3.
Equate imaginary parts: y plus 4 equals minus 2 so y equals minus 6.
So the answer is x equals 3, y equals minus 6.

heading.en: Powers of i: use the remainder

body.en: Divide the exponent by 4 and keep the remainder r. Then iⁿ = iʳ: remainder 0 → 1, 1 → i, 2 → −1, 3 → −i. For negative n, add a multiple of 4 first.

say.en: Powers of i: use the remainder. Divide the exponent by 4 and keep the remainder r. Then i to the power n equals i to the power r: remainder 0 gives 1, 1 gives i, 2 gives minus 1, 3 gives -i. For negative n, add a multiple of 4 first.
